title: Divisorial charts of a regular strict normal crossings pair
statement: Let $Y$ be a regular Noetherian scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth] and $T\subset Y$ a strict normal crossings boundary [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], allowing $T=\varnothing$. Put $V=Y\setminus|T|$. The divisorial log structure $M_Y=\mathcal O_Y\cap j_*\mathcal O_V^\times$, where $j:V\hookrightarrow Y$, makes $(Y,M_Y)$ a locally Noetherian fine saturated log scheme [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] with triviality locus $V$. At each geometric point $\bar y$, with strict local ring $A$, it admits a pointed etale-local chart $\mathbf N^r\to M_Y$ identifying $\mathbf N^r$ with its characteristic monoid at $\bar y$. The standard generators map to $t_1,\ldots,t_r$ forming part of a regular system of parameters of $A$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. In this chart the ideal generated by nonunits of $M_{Y,\bar y}$ is $(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$, its quotient is regular, and $\dim A=\dim A/(t_1,\ldots,t_r)+r$. In particular $(Y,T)$ is a log regular pair [def-trf-log-regular-pair]. No field base or excellence assumption is imposed.

source.place: Expose VI 1.2--1.5(i), printed pp. 69--70; IX 2.1, printed p. 133 (regular normal crossings pair); VIII Remark 4.2.2(i), printed p. 118 (regular-intersection boundary criterion).

proof.text: Fix an ordinary point $y\in Y$, and let $R=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ have dimension $d$. By [def-weil-regular-scheme], $R$ is Noetherian regular local. Enumerate the boundary components through $y$ as $C_1,\ldots,C_r$, and remove the other finitely many components. Write $I_i\subset R$ for the ideal of $C_i$ at $y$. By [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], $R/I_i$ is regular of dimension $d-1$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-quotient-kernel-parameters] to $I_i$: it is generated by the first $c_i$ members of some parameter system. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], its quotient has dimension $d-c_i$. Thus $c_i=1$; choose a generator $t_i$. These are separate choices for the individual component ideals, not yet a simultaneous parameter system.

source.place: Tag 00NR, lemma-regular-quotient-regular; Tag 00NQ, lemma-regular-ring-CM; ILO VIII Remark 4.2.2(i).

proof.text: Represent these finitely many germs by functions on one affine open neighbourhood $W$ of $y$. Shrink $W$ so that $C_i\cap W=V(t_i)$ for every $i$. Here the ideals on an affine Noetherian neighbourhood are finitely generated: write $t_i$ in the component ideal after clearing its germ denominator, and write each ideal generator as a multiple of $t_i$ in $R$; the finitely many equations hold after inverting one element outside the prime of $y$. This gives the claimed equality of ideals on a neighbourhood. Put $T_0=t_1\cdots t_r$; since the boundary support is the union of the component supports, $V\cap W=D(T_0)$. For $r=0$ take $T_0=1$ and $W\subset V$. On each ordinary local ring of $W$, each component equation vanishing there is a parameter by Step 1 and hence nonzero by [lem-sc-regular-local-domain]; the others are units. Thus the local product is nonzero. To see density, apply this at the generic point of any irreducible component of $W$: its regular local ring is a field, so $T_0$ is invertible there. Hence $D(T_0)$ contains all generic points and is dense. These neighbourhoods cover $Y$, proving that $V$ is dense.

source.place: VI 1.4 and VIII Remark 4.2.2(i); explicit finite-generator neighbourhood argument for component equations.

proof.text: Let $p$ be any point of this fixed $W$, put $J=\{i:t_i(p)=0\}$ and $s=|J|$, and set $(R_p,\mathfrak m,\kappa)=\mathcal O_{Y,p}$ and $d_p=\dim R_p$. By [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], the intersection of the $C_i$ for $i\in J$ has regular local ring $R_p/I$, where $I=(t_i:i\in J)$, and dimension $d_p-s$. The cotangent surjection $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2\to(\mathfrak m/I)/(\mathfrak m/I)^2$ has kernel $(I+\mathfrak m^2)/\mathfrak m^2$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension] its dimension is $d_p-(d_p-s)=s$. The $s$ classes of our actual $t_i$ span that kernel, so they are linearly independent. Extend them to a basis of $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ and lift the remaining vectors to $R_p$. By [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] these $d_p$ lifts generate the maximal ideal. Thus the actual $t_i$, $i\in J$, extend to a regular system of parameters [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. This also handles $J=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 00NR, lemma-regular-quotient-regular, cotangent calculation; Tag 00KU, definition-regular-local; Tag 00DV, lemma-NAK. The dimension hypothesis is the local version in ILO VIII Remark 4.2.2(i).

proof.text: For a geometric point $\bar p$ over $p\in W$, [lem-exc-affine-strict-local-ring-comparison] identifies its strict local ring $A$ with $R_p^{\mathrm{sh}}$, compatibly with the functions on $W$. By [lem-sc-strict-henselization-regular], $A$ is Noetherian regular local. The cotangent isomorphism of [lem-sc-strict-henselization-cotangent-dimension] carries the full basis of Step 3 to a basis after extending the residue field. Nakayama [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] shows that its lifts generate the maximal ideal of $A$, and [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension] gives $\dim A=d_p$. Hence the same $t_i$, $i\in J$, are part of a parameter system of $A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], $A/(t_i:i\in J)$ is regular of dimension $\dim A-s$. This is verified at every geometric point of $W$, not just at the chosen centre.

source.place: Tag 06LN, lemma-henselization-regular, statement and minimal-generator proof; algebra.tex Tag 00NQ, lemma-regular-ring-CM; etale-cohomology.tex Tag 04HX, lemma-describe-etale-local-ring.

proof.text: The formula for $M_Y$ in [def-trf-log-regular-pair] is a sheaf of multiplicative monoids: its sections are regular functions invertible on the inverse image of $V$, a condition local for the etale topology. Its inclusion into $\mathcal O_Y$ identifies its inverse image of $\mathcal O_Y^\times$ with $\mathcal O_Y^\times$, so this is a log structure [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Compute its stalk at $\bar p$ using [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. A divisorial section on an affine pointed etale neighbourhood has an inverse after inverting $T_0$, and therefore gives $f\in A$ invertible in $A[1/T_0]$. Conversely such an $f$ has an equation $fg=T_0^n$ in $A$ for some $g\in A,n\ge0$: a localization inverse, multiplied by a further power of $T_0$, gives this equation. Represent $f,g$ and this one equality on a common pointed neighbourhood, by the ring colimit description of the stalk in [lem-exc-affine-strict-local-ring-comparison]. There the inverse of $f$ on $D(T_0)$ is $g/T_0^n$, so $f$ is a divisorial germ. Equality of germs in $A$ likewise holds after refinement, proving injectivity. Thus $M_{Y,\bar p}=\{f\in A:f\in A[1/T_0]^\times\}$. The same finite equation with $n=0$ identifies the unit-sheaf stalk with $A^\times$.

source.place: VI 1.1 and 1.4, printed p. 69; explicit finite-witness stalk calculation; etale-cohomology.tex Tag 04HX, lemma-describe-etale-local-ring.

proof.text: Every $t_i$ is invertible on $D(T_0)$, so the chosen sections define $\alpha:P=\mathbf N^r\to M_Y(W)$. At $\bar p$ put $K=\{1,\ldots,r\}\setminus J$. The $t_i$ for $i\in K$ are units of $A$. For $i\in J$ they are distinct members of a parameter system by Step 4. By [lem-trf-regular-local-ufd-boundary-factorization] and Step 5, every element of $M_{Y,\bar p}$ has the form $u\prod_{i\in J}t_i^{a_i}$ with $u\in A^\times$ and $a_i\in\mathbf N$. The prime parameters are pairwise nonassociate: association would make two cotangent basis vectors proportional. Unique factorization therefore makes both their exponents and the unit coefficient unique.

source.place: Tag 0AG0, lemma-regular-local-UFD; localization-unit consequence. ILO IX 2.1 proof, printed p. 133, chart by boundary parameters.

proof.text: A product is a unit in a commutative ring only if each factor is a unit. Consequently $\alpha^{-1}(A^\times)=\mathbf N^K$. In the chart pushout of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], the map $(n,u)\mapsto(n|_J,u\prod_{i\in K}t_i^{n_i})$ identifies $P\oplus_{\mathbf N^K}A^\times$ with $\mathbf N^J\oplus A^\times$: its inverse inserts zero in the $K$ coordinates. The relations of the pushout are exactly absorption of these unit coordinates into $u$. Step 6 identifies the latter monoid with $M_{Y,\bar p}$. Thus $P\to M_Y(W)$ satisfies the chart condition at every geometric point of $W$. Modulo the units its characteristic is $\mathbf N^J$. At the selected centre $\bar y$, all $r$ component equations vanish, so $J=\{1,\ldots,r\}$ and this chart identifies $\mathbf N^r$ with the characteristic at $\bar y$. Since the open immersion $W\hookrightarrow Y$ is etale, this is the required pointed etale-local chart.

source.place: VI 1.1 and 1.5(i), pp. 69--70; IX 2.1 proof, p. 133; explicit chart-pushout calculation.

proof.text: The monoid $\mathbf N^r$ is finitely generated by its basis, embeds in $\mathbf Z^r$, and is saturated: if $ng$ has nonnegative coordinates for $n>0$, then so does $g$. Hence these are fine saturated charts in the sense of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. The characteristic $\mathbf N^J$ is zero exactly when $J$ is empty, precisely off the boundary, so the triviality locus is $V$. In the description of Step 6, a monomial is a nonunit exactly when some exponent is positive. Thus its ideal of nonunits is exactly $(t_i:i\in J)$: each nonunit is divisible by such a $t_i$, and each $t_i$ for $i\in J$ is a nonunit. Step 4 gives regularity of the quotient and $\dim A=\dim A/(t_i:i\in J)+|J|$. Its characteristic group is $\mathbf Z^J$ of rank $|J|$, proving exactly log regularity as defined in [def-trf-log-regular-pair]. The underlying scheme is locally Noetherian by hypothesis. At the centre this is the claimed ideal $(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$ and dimension formula. For an empty boundary, $r=0$, the chart is the zero monoid, $M_Y=\mathcal O_Y^\times$, the ideal is zero and the dimension equality is tautological. All arguments used Noetherian regularity and the stated intersection conditions; none used a field base or excellence.

source.place: VI 1.1--1.5(i), pp. 69--70, and IX 2.1, p. 133; elementary coordinate verification of the log-regularity definition.
